questions.q: What's the real advantage of an alert over checking the Monitor hub manually?
options: It notifies you the moment a condition is met, without you having to go looking
Alerts replace the Monitor hub entirely
Alerts only work for trigger runs, not pipeline runs
There's no real difference — both require checking the portal
questions.explain: Alerts push a notification to you when a defined condition is met, so a production failure doesn't sit unnoticed until someone happens to check the runs list.

questions.q: Which of these is a real, selectable alert metric in Data Factory?
options: Failed activity runs metrics
Total number of linked services created
Number of datasets in the factory
Average pipeline name length
questions.explain: Data Factory offers metrics for failed/cancelled activity, pipeline, and trigger runs, plus integration runtime health metrics like CPU utilization and available memory.

questions.q: How do you scope an alert to only one specific pipeline instead of the whole data factory?
options: Filter the alert logic by the PipelineName dimension
Alerts always apply to the entire data factory with no scoping possible
Create a separate data factory for that one pipeline
Rename the pipeline to match the alert rule's name
questions.explain: The Configure alert logic screen lets you filter by dimensions like ActivityType, ActivityName, and PipelineName, so a single critical pipeline can have its own tightly-scoped alert.

questions.q: What does the `retry` property in an activity's policy block control?
options: The maximum number of times the activity automatically retries after failing
How many pipelines can run at the same time
The number of datasets an activity can reference
How many alerts can be attached to the activity
questions.explain: The retry property sets the maximum retry attempts for an activity, with a default of 0 — meaning no automatic retries unless you explicitly opt in.

questions.q: Why would setting `secureOutput: true` on an activity's policy matter?
options: It prevents the activity's output from being logged for monitoring, useful for sensitive data
It encrypts the activity's connection to its linked service
It automatically retries the activity on any failure
It hides the activity from the Monitor hub entirely
questions.explain: secureOutput marks the activity's output as sensitive so it isn't captured in monitoring logs, without disabling monitoring for the activity as a whole.
